items.question: What is MotoVault?
items.answer: MotoVault is a free iOS and Android app that keeps a rider's records in one place: maintenance history with reminders, per-bike expenses, recorded rides and multi-day trip plans with GPX export. The bike catalogue covers 12,000+ models from the NHTSA vehicle database. No OBD hardware, and no subscription to start.

items.question: Is MotoVault really free?
items.answer: Yes. One bike in your garage, full maintenance tracking with service history, expense logging, ride recording and the trip planner are free, with no trial and no card. Pro is a monthly or yearly subscription, with a lifetime option; prices are shown in the store and on /pro. It unlocks unlimited bikes, receipt scans, GPX exports and offline trip maps.

items.question: How does AI diagnostics work?
items.answer: MotoVault reads the photo with a vision model. Open the diagnostic camera in the app, frame the part, warning light or area of concern, and tap the shutter. The model names what it sees, lists the likely causes for your bike's make and model, and returns a diagnosis with a severity estimate and a recommended next step. Each result carries a confidence level of low, medium or high; treat it as a first opinion and confirm anything safety-critical with a mechanic. The full answer is saved to the bike's history.

items.question: What motorcycles does MotoVault support?
items.answer: MotoVault's catalogue covers every major motorcycle make and model from the last 30 years, 12,000+ models in all, sourced from the NHTSA Vehicle Product Information Catalog, the United States federal database for vehicle identification. Coverage spans Honda, Yamaha, Kawasaki, Suzuki, BMW, Ducati, KTM, Harley-Davidson, Triumph, Royal Enfield, Aprilia and Indian. Pick the make, model and year; then set each service interval once and the app counts down from your odometer. If your model is not listed, add it manually with your own intervals. Source: NHTSA Vehicle Product Information Catalog, maintained by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.

items.question: Is my data safe?
items.answer: Your records — GPS traces, maintenance entries, expenses and diagnostic photos — are stored on EU servers, encrypted in transit and at rest, and deleted on request. Each rider can read only their own records, down to the database layer. MotoVault does not sell rider data. You can delete your account from the app. Details: /privacy.

items.question: How does trip planning work?
items.answer: MotoVault trip planning builds multi-day motorcycle routes on a live map with real road routing. Waypoints are typed — fuel, food, overnight, scenic, photo, mechanical, ferry, pass summit, rally point and stop — and each type has its own icon on the map. Invite the riders who are coming, and when the plan is final export it as a standard GPX file for a Garmin, TomTom or any unit that reads GPX. Trip planning and saved routes are unlimited on the free tier; MotoVault Pro adds unlimited GPX exports and unlimited AI trip-assistant questions.

items.question: Can I use MotoVault offline?
items.answer: MotoVault works offline for the features that matter most when you are on the road without cell service. Ride recording continues to log GPS coordinates, speed, elevation, and duration using your phone sensors with no data connection required. You can also log maintenance entries and expenses while offline, and all entries will sync automatically once your device reconnects. Trip plans that were previously loaded are available for viewing offline as well. The data synchronization is conflict-free, meaning edits made offline and online will merge cleanly without data loss. The one feature that requires an active internet connection is AI diagnostics, because the image must reach the cloud-based vision model for analysis. All other core functions work reliably in remote areas.

items.question: How is MotoVault different from REVER or Calimoto?
items.answer: REVER and Calimoto plan and navigate routes. MotoVault keeps the bike's records — rides, service history, costs — and plans multi-day trips; it does not navigate. Recorded rides move the odometer, so service reminders count down on their own, and every expense sits against its bike. For turn-by-turn directions, export the GPX and copy it into your planner.

items.question: What maintenance reminders does MotoVault send?
items.answer: By distance or by time, whichever comes first: oil and filter, chain, tyres, brake pads, coolant, valve clearance, air filter, spark plugs. Set each interval once for your bike and the app counts down from the odometer; recorded rides move the odometer, so the countdown moves with them. Add jobs unique to your bike at any time.

items.question: Can I track expenses for multiple bikes?
items.answer: The free tier covers one bike; Pro unlocks unlimited bikes. Every expense sits against the bike it belongs to, in one of 14 categories: fuel, insurance, parts, gear, service and more. Each bike shows its running total and its cost per kilometre, so you can see what each one really costs to run.

items.question: Does MotoVault work with OBD-II scanners?
items.answer: MotoVault does not require OBD-II hardware, Bluetooth adapters, diagnostic cables, or any external scanning device. The AI diagnostic feature works entirely through your smartphone camera, which means you can photograph a part, warning light, fluid leak, or any visible issue and receive an AI-generated assessment without purchasing additional equipment. This approach was chosen deliberately because most motorcycles either lack standard OBD-II ports, use proprietary diagnostic connectors, or require manufacturer-specific scan tools that cost hundreds of dollars. By using computer vision instead of hardware protocols, MotoVault diagnostics works on any motorcycle regardless of age, manufacturer, or electronic sophistication. Simply point your camera at the concern, and the AI vision model analyzes what it sees against known failure patterns for your specific bike.

items.question: Can I export routes as GPX?
items.answer: Yes. Trips you plan in MotoVault export as standard GPX route files, which import directly into Garmin Zumo, TomTom Rider, Hammerhead Karoo, or any GPS navigation unit that accepts GPX. Exported files follow the GPX 1.1 specification and work with Google Earth, Komoot, Basecamp and other third-party tools without modification. Free accounts include one GPX export per month of a published route on the web; MotoVault Pro unlocks unlimited exports, including your own trips in the app. Recorded rides stay in your ride history and can't be exported as GPX yet.

items.question: What countries are motorcycle routes available in?
items.answer: Routes on /explore are grouped by country and region; each one shows distance, climb, riding time and surface, and opens on a map. Coverage follows the curated routes published so far, strongest in Europe and North America, and grows as new regions are added.

items.question: How accurate is the AI diagnostic feature?
items.answer: MotoVault AI diagnostics provides each assessment with a confidence rating of low, medium, or high so you can judge reliability at a glance. High-confidence results typically involve clearly visible issues like worn brake pads, damaged chain links, leaking fluids with identifiable color, or standard dashboard warning lights. Medium-confidence results indicate the AI detected a probable issue but recommends professional verification. Low-confidence results mean the image was ambiguous or the issue requires physical inspection beyond what is visible in a photograph. The AI diagnostic feature is explicitly not a replacement for a qualified motorcycle mechanic. It is best used for identifying potential issues before they worsen, understanding what dashboard warning lights mean for your specific model, and deciding whether a problem requires immediate attention or can wait until your next scheduled service appointment.

Privacy.title: Privacy policy
Privacy.intro: MotoVault is operated by Kan Consult s.r.o. ('we', 'us', 'our'). We respect your privacy and are committed to protecting your personal data. This Privacy Policy explains how Kan Consult s.r.o., a company established in the Slovak Republic (European Union) and the operator of MotoVault, collects, uses, discloses, and safeguards information when you use the MotoVault mobile application, the motovault.app website, and related services (together, the 'Service'). For purposes of the EU/UK General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), Kan Consult s.r.o. is the data controller of your personal data. If you have any questions about this policy or our data practices, contact us at support@motovault.app.
Privacy.infoCollect: We collect the following categories of personal information: (1) Account & authentication data — email address, display name, profile photo, and federated identifiers when you sign in via Supabase Auth (Google, Apple, or email/password); (2) Motorcycle & garage data — make, model, year, VIN, mileage, maintenance records, expenses, and photos you add to your garage; (3) Diagnostic images & inputs — photos and descriptions you submit for AI-assisted diagnostic analysis; images are processed in real time and not stored permanently after analysis; (4) Location & ride data — when you use trip planning, the ride logging HUD, GPX export, or 'Explore Routes', we process precise GPS coordinates, speed, heading, altitude, distance, duration, and ride traces. Location is collected only while the relevant feature is active and only after you grant explicit operating-system permission; (5) Community & user-generated content — public rider handle, profile bio, posts, comments, likes, follows, photos, and routes you choose to share with the community; (6) Subscription & purchase data — receipts, subscription status, and entitlement information processed through Apple App Store and Google Play; we do not store full payment-card numbers on our servers; (7) Usage analytics — feature interactions, screens viewed, performance metrics, and aggregated engagement signals collected via PostHog; (8) Crash & error data — stack traces, device state, and error context collected via Sentry; (9) Device & technical data — device model, operating system, app version, language, time zone, IP address, and device identifiers needed for authentication and security; (10) Communications — emails, support tickets, and feedback you send us.
Privacy.howWeUse: We use your information to: (1) provide, operate, and maintain the Service, including account management, the garage, AI diagnostics, learning content, ride logging, trip planning, route exploration, and community features; (2) process subscription purchases and manage entitlements; (3) personalize your experience and remember your preferences; (4) generate AI-assisted diagnostic results and educational content; (5) communicate with you about service updates, security alerts, and important policy changes, and (with your consent where required) product news; (6) understand how the Service is used so we can improve features, performance, and reliability; (7) detect, investigate, and prevent fraud, abuse, security incidents, and violations of our Terms; (8) comply with legal obligations, enforce our agreements, and respond to lawful requests from public authorities. We do not sell your personal data, and we do not share it for cross-context behavioural advertising. We do not rent your data to third parties for their own marketing purposes.
Privacy.legalBasis: If you are in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or Switzerland, we process your personal data under the following lawful bases of GDPR Article 6: (1) Performance of a contract — to create and operate your account, deliver the features you request (garage, diagnostics, ride logging, trip planning), and provide subscription benefits; (2) Consent — for processing that requires opt-in, including precise location collection, push notifications, optional marketing emails, and non-essential analytics or cookies. You can withdraw consent at any time without affecting prior lawful processing; (3) Legitimate interests — to secure the Service, prevent fraud and abuse, debug crashes, conduct aggregated analytics, and improve our products, where these interests are not overridden by your rights and freedoms; (4) Legal obligations — to comply with tax, accounting, consumer protection, and law-enforcement obligations under Slovak and EU law. We do not use the Service to make solely automated decisions producing legal or similarly significant effects on you within the meaning of GDPR Article 22.
Privacy.thirdParty: We share personal data only with vetted service providers who act as our processors and are bound by written data-processing agreements. Current sub-processors include: (1) Supabase — database, authentication, and file storage (EU/US regions); (2) Anthropic — Claude AI for diagnostic and educational content generation (United States; submitted data is not used to train foundation models); (3) Mapbox — maps, geocoding, and route rendering for trip planning and explore (United States); (4) Sentry — application error and crash monitoring (United States/EU); (5) PostHog — product analytics and feature usage telemetry (EU region); (6) Apple App Store and Google Play — in-app purchases and subscriptions; (7) a transactional email provider — service-related emails; (8) NHTSA vPIC — public motorcycle catalog (no personal data shared). We may also disclose information when required by law, in response to lawful requests by public authorities, to protect our rights and the safety of our users, or in connection with a corporate transaction (e.g., merger, acquisition) where the recipient agrees to honor this Privacy Policy. An up-to-date list of sub-processors is available on request.
Privacy.cookies: Our website uses cookies and similar technologies (local storage, session storage, device identifiers) to keep you signed in, remember preferences such as language, measure aggregated traffic, and protect against fraud. Strictly necessary cookies are set by default. Analytics and other non-essential cookies are loaded only after you provide consent through our cookie banner where required by EU/UK ePrivacy rules. You can withdraw consent at any time via 'Cookie Settings' in the website footer or by clearing cookies in your browser. The mobile app uses native device identifiers and on-device storage rather than HTTP cookies; you can reset advertising identifiers in your device settings.
Privacy.dataRetention: We retain personal data only as long as necessary for the purposes described above or as required by law: (1) Account profile and garage data — kept while your account is active; deleted within 30 days of account deletion (with up to 90 days in encrypted backups); (2) Ride and location data — kept while your account is active; you can delete individual rides at any time; (3) Diagnostic images — processed and deleted within 24 hours of analysis; only the resulting text-based diagnosis is kept with your account; (4) Subscription and billing records — retained for the period required by Slovak tax and accounting law (currently up to 10 years for invoices); (5) Usage analytics — retained for up to 12 months in identifiable form, then aggregated; (6) Crash and error logs — retained for up to 90 days; (7) Support communications — retained for up to 24 months after the issue is closed; (8) Backups — disaster-recovery backups are rotated within 30 days. Where required by law (litigation hold, regulatory request, fraud investigation), we may retain specific records for longer.
Privacy.security: We implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect personal data, including: TLS 1.2+ encryption in transit; encryption at rest for databases and file storage; JWT authentication validated locally; secure native key storage on mobile (expo-secure-store; never AsyncStorage); least-privilege access controls and audit logging for staff; mandatory security training; and regular dependency, infrastructure, and code-review processes. Despite these safeguards, no system can guarantee absolute security. If we become aware of a personal data breach that is likely to result in a risk to your rights and freedoms, we will notify the competent supervisory authority (the Slovak Office for Personal Data Protection) without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware, in line with GDPR Articles 33–34. Where the breach is likely to result in a high risk to your rights and freedoms, we will also notify affected users without undue delay.

UK users can complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO). California residents have additional CCPA/CPRA rights: the right to know what personal information we collect and how it is used and shared, the right to delete, the right to correct, the right to opt out of 'sale' or 'sharing' of personal information (we do not sell or share for cross-context behavioural advertising), and the right to limit the use of sensitive personal information (which includes precise geolocation). California residents may exercise these rights at support@motovault.app and may designate an authorized agent. We will not discriminate against you for exercising any of these rights. We respond to verifiable requests within 30 days for GDPR (extendable by up to 60 additional days for complex requests) and within 45 days for CCPA/CPRA (extendable by 45 additional days with notice).

faq.question: How does AI motorcycle diagnostics work without OBD?
faq.answer: MotoVault uses advanced photo-based diagnosis powered by AI. Simply take a photo of the issue or describe your symptoms, and our AI analyzes the image to identify components, detect wear patterns, spot fluid leaks, and assess damage severity. Unlike OBD scanners that read error codes through a port, MotoVault uses visual recognition — meaning it works on every motorcycle regardless of age or make, with no adapters or cables required.

faq.question: What motorcycle problems can MotoVault diagnose?
faq.answer: MotoVault can diagnose a wide range of issues including engine problems (overheating, oil leaks, unusual noises), electrical system faults (dead batteries, faulty wiring, blown fuses), brake wear and pad thickness, tire condition and tread depth, suspension leaks and sag, chain tension and sprocket wear, fluid leaks and contamination, corrosion and body damage, and dashboard warning lights. Each diagnosis includes a severity rating so you know what needs immediate attention.

faq.question: Is AI motorcycle diagnostics accurate?
faq.answer: Every result carries a confidence level. Treat it as a first opinion: it tells you what the problem most likely is and what to check next. Confirm anything safety-critical — brakes, steering, structural damage — with a mechanic before you ride.

faq.question: Do I need special equipment for AI diagnostics?
faq.answer: No special equipment is needed — just your smartphone camera. MotoVault is designed to work with the camera already in your pocket. Take a clear, well-lit photo of the part or issue, and the AI handles the rest. No OBD adapters, no Bluetooth dongles, no proprietary tools. This makes MotoVault accessible to every rider regardless of technical experience or budget.

faq.question: How is MotoVault different from OBD2 scanners?
faq.answer: Traditional OBD2 scanners only work on bikes with an OBD port (mostly newer models), require a physical adapter, and can only read stored error codes. MotoVault works on any motorcycle — vintage, modern, carbureted, or fuel-injected — because it uses visual AI analysis instead of electronic port reading. It can identify problems that OBD scanners miss entirely, such as physical wear, corrosion, fluid leaks, and tire condition. Plus, MotoVault provides plain-language explanations instead of cryptic error codes.

FeaturesDiagnostics.longFormIntro: Motorcycle diagnostics has traditionally been the domain of experienced mechanics with specialized tools. MotoVault changes that by putting AI-powered diagnostic capabilities directly in your pocket. Whether you are a seasoned rider who has been wrenching for decades or a new rider who just bought their first bike, MotoVault's AI diagnostics helps you understand what is happening with your motorcycle — quickly, accurately, and without expensive equipment.
FeaturesDiagnostics.longFormHow: A vision model reads the photo, identifies components and wear patterns, and reasons about them for your specific make, model and year. Severity runs from minor to critical, and every result carries a confidence level: it is a first opinion, not a verdict. The bike catalogue covers 12,000+ models.
FeaturesDiagnostics.longFormExamples: Riders use MotoVault diagnostics in countless real-world scenarios. A rider notices a puddle under their parked bike — they snap a photo and MotoVault identifies it as a coolant leak from the water pump seal, rated as moderate severity with a recommendation to replace the seal before the next long ride. Another rider sees a dashboard warning light they do not recognize — a quick photo identifies it as a lean fuel mixture indicator, likely caused by a dirty air filter. A new rider inspecting their used purchase photographs the chain — MotoVault detects excessive stretch and worn sprocket teeth, recommending a full chain and sprocket replacement. These are the kinds of everyday situations where having an AI mechanic in your pocket saves time, money, and prevents breakdowns.
FeaturesDiagnostics.longFormComparison: Traditional motorcycle diagnostics relies on OBD2 scanners (limited to newer bikes with compatible ports), multimeters for electrical testing, and the trained eye of an experienced mechanic. MotoVault does not replace these tools — it gives you an accessible first opinion. Where an OBD scanner reads stored error codes, MotoVault sees problems that have no error code: worn brake pads, corroded terminals, leaking fork seals, or a chain that needs adjustment. Each result carries a confidence level, so you know how much weight to give it. The result is a more informed decision about your motorcycle — whether you fix it yourself or take it to a shop with a clear description of the problem.
FeaturesDiagnostics.scanBody: Slack measures ~45mm. Adjust to 25–35mm at the rear axle pivot. Estimated 8 minutes with standard tools.
FeaturesDiagnostics.step1Body: Open the MotoVault camera and point at a warning light, a leak, the source of an odd noise, or a part you don't recognise. No special framing — any angle works.
FeaturesDiagnostics.step2Body: A vision model identifies the part, then cross-references your bike’s make, model and year against known failure modes. All on-device where possible; cloud fallback for edge cases.
FeaturesDiagnostics.step3Body: Get a diagnosis, difficulty rating, estimated time and step-by-step fix. Save to your bike’s history with one tap. Or share the scan with your mechanic before you even roll in.

FeaturesDiagnostics.resultDemoBody: A sample result for a chain that has gone slack. Every diagnosis is saved to the bike's record, so the next time the same symptom shows up you can see what you did about it.

faq.question: What topics are covered in the learning paths?
faq.answer: MotoVault's learning paths cover a wide range of motorcycle maintenance topics including oil changes and fluid management, brake pad inspection and replacement, chain cleaning, lubrication and adjustment, tire care and pressure monitoring, electrical system basics and battery maintenance, seasonal preparation and storage, suspension setup and tuning, and engine fundamentals. New articles are added based on rider feedback.

faq.question: Is this suitable for beginners with no mechanical experience?
faq.answer: Yes. MotoVault's learning paths start with the fundamentals and you do not need any prior mechanical experience. Each module begins with the basic concepts — what the parts are, why they matter and how they work — before moving on to the maintenance tasks themselves, with step-by-step instructions and an explanation of the why behind each procedure.

faq.question: How long does each lesson take?
faq.answer: Most lessons are designed to take between 5 and 15 minutes, making them easy to fit into a busy schedule. Shorter lessons cover single concepts or quick tips, while longer lessons include more detailed walkthroughs and hands-on exercises. You can pause and resume at any time — your progress is saved automatically.

faq.question: Are there practical exercises included?
faq.answer: Not as separate exercises. The articles describe each procedure on your own motorcycle — the steps, the tools and what to look for — and each module ends with a quiz on what you have read.

faq.question: Can I track my learning progress?
faq.answer: Yes. Each module shows what you have read and what is next, and your quiz results are kept with it, so you can see where you stand and which topic to open next.

FeaturesLearning.longFormTitle: Structured motorcycle learning, from beginner to expert
FeaturesLearning.longFormIntro: Learning motorcycle maintenance should not feel overwhelming. MotoVault's learning paths break down complex mechanical knowledge into digestible, structured courses that take you from complete beginner to confident home mechanic. Whether you want to perform basic maintenance like oil changes and chain adjustments, or dive deeper into engine internals and suspension tuning, there is a path designed for your skill level.
FeaturesLearning.longFormCurriculum: The four modules build on one another rather than standing as isolated tips: what a part does comes before how to service it, and how to service it before how to tune it. Routine maintenance covers the jobs every rider meets; engine internals, electrical systems and suspension tuning go deeper into the systems behind them.
FeaturesLearning.longFormProgression: The modules run in order, from fundamentals to the jobs that save a shop visit. Beginners start with foundational knowledge — understanding what each part of their motorcycle does and why maintenance matters. Intermediate readers tackle procedures with step-by-step instructions. Advanced content covers diagnostics and tuning. The order means you are never thrown into content that is too advanced, and never asked to re-read material you already know.
FeaturesLearning.longFormLesson: Each lesson follows a proven format designed for retention and practical application. Lessons begin with a clear learning objective — what you will understand or be able to do after completing it. Visual explanations with diagrams and annotated photos make complex systems easy to understand. Key concepts are highlighted and reinforced through interactive quizzes that test comprehension in real time. Many lessons conclude with a practical exercise: a guided, step-by-step task you perform on your own motorcycle, complete with safety reminders and tool requirements. This combination of theory and practice means you do not just memorize facts — you build real skills you can use in your garage. The AI adapts explanations to your specific bike when possible, making the content directly relevant to the motorcycle you ride.

faq.question: What maintenance records can I log?
faq.answer: MotoVault logs a wide range of maintenance tasks including oil and filter changes, tire replacements and rotations, brake pad and fluid service, chain cleaning, lubrication and replacement, coolant and hydraulic fluid changes, valve adjustments, spark plug replacements, battery replacements, and custom tasks for any service specific to your bike. Each record includes the date, odometer reading, cost, notes and optional photos.

faq.question: Does MotoVault remind me about upcoming maintenance?
faq.answer: Yes. Reminders go by distance, by date, or both — set an oil change every 5,000 miles or every 6 months, whichever comes first. Reminders are set per bike and per task, so your sport bike and touring bike can follow different schedules.

faq.question: Can I track maintenance expenses?
faq.answer: Yes. Every maintenance record can include cost information, and MotoVault provides expense tracking with categories and summaries. You can see total spending per bike, cost breakdowns by maintenance type, monthly and yearly expense trends, and cost-per-mile calculations. This data is invaluable for budgeting and for documenting your investment when it comes time to sell.

faq.question: Is my garage data backed up and synced?
faq.answer: Yes. Your records are stored on EU servers (Supabase), encrypted in transit and at rest, and deleted on request; details at /privacy. Sign in on a new phone and your garage is there.

FeaturesGarage.longFormTitle: Garage management that keeps every bike on track
FeaturesGarage.longFormIntro: Owning a motorcycle means staying on top of maintenance — and if you own more than one, keeping track of service schedules, part replacements and expenses becomes a real job. MotoVault's garage gives you one organised place for every bike you own, with complete service histories, reminders you set by distance or date, and expense tracking.
FeaturesGarage.longFormMultiBike: Whether you ride a single daily commuter or keep a collection, MotoVault's garage scales to fit. Each bike is stored with its specifications — make, model, year, VIN and current odometer reading. Compare maintenance costs across bikes, see which motorcycle needs attention next, and keep every record in one place instead of scattered across notebooks, spreadsheets and shoe boxes of receipts.
FeaturesGarage.longFormScheduling: Oil changes every 5,000 miles or 6 months. Chain lubrication every 500 miles. Tire inspection every spring. Coolant flush every 2 years. Each reminder is customizable per bike, because your sportbike and your touring bike have different needs. When you complete a maintenance task, log it and the next reminder is scheduled automatically. No more guessing when you last changed the oil or whether the brake fluid is overdue.
FeaturesGarage.longFormResale: A complete, documented service history is one of the most valuable things you can show a buyer. MotoVault's garage keeps a verifiable record of every service performed on your motorcycle — dates, odometer readings, costs, parts used and notes. When it comes time to sell, you can share the bike's service history as a read-only web link that shows responsible ownership and supports your asking price. Even if you never plan to sell, a complete record helps you spot patterns, plan ahead for major services and make sure nothing is forgotten.

Butler Maps integration, friend tracking, and curated community routes make it feel like the Strava of motorcycling. REVER Pro at around $39.99 a year adds offline maps and turn-by-turn navigation. CompareAlternatives.bestFor3Body: If you're iPhone-only and your single requirement is zero-effort ride capture, RideLog is a legitimately strong pick. Its automatic ride detection using iPhone motion sensors is excellent, and the Dynamic Island and Find-My-Motorcycle integrations feel very native. It also covers basic maintenance and expense logging — so for a solo iPhone rider who doesn't need AI diagnostics, Android support, or trip planning, it can genuinely be enough. Caveat: multiple unrelated apps share the RideLog name across both stores, so double-check you're looking at the motorcycle variant before subscribing.
CompareAlternatives.bestFor4Body: MotorManage is the app we’d recommend to a wrench-focused rider who wants a deep vehicle database and a clean service log and specifically does not want the complexity of rides, community, or diagnostics. Its OEM spec data and parts catalog are genuinely well-curated. The free plan covers two motorcycles and the King upgrade is €3.99 a month or €29.99 a year, which some riders prefer to a broader subscription. The trade-off: no rides, no navigation, no AI, and no learning content. MotoVault covers the same garage ground and adds everything MotorManage deliberately leaves out — so choose MotorManage only if minimalism is a feature for you.
CompareAlternatives.whenToChooseCompetitor: We'd recommend a specialist over MotoVault in three specific situations. First: if dedicated offline turn-by-turn navigation is your single biggest requirement — Calimoto or REVER Pro cover that territory better. Second: if passive iPhone-only ride detection is your hard requirement and you don't want to start rides manually — RideLog's motion-sensor approach wins on pure ergonomics. Third: if you genuinely only want a vehicle database with OEM specs and zero ancillary features — MotorManage stays out of your way. If your bike isn’t supported, if you’re not comfortable clearing codes yourself, or if you mostly want maintenance tracking and symptom help, skip the hardware and start with MotoVault’s AI diagnostics.

FeaturesTripPlanning.title: Motorcycle trip planner: multi-day routes and GPX export
FeaturesTripPlanning.description: Plan multi-day motorcycle trips with typed waypoints and real road routing, invite riders, export GPX. Free on iOS and Android.
FeaturesTripPlanning.heroTitle: Plan every mile of the ride
FeaturesTripPlanning.heroSubtitle: Multi-day routes with typed waypoints and real road routing on a live map: the first feature we built, and the one that shapes the rest.
FeaturesTripPlanning.seoHeading: A motorcycle trip planner for multi-day routes
FeaturesTripPlanning.seoIntro: MotoVault is a motorcycle trip planning app for multi-day tours. Build a route with typed waypoints — fuel, food, scenic stops, overnights, passes, ferries — on a live map with real motorcycle-friendly road routing. Invite riders, share the link, export GPX for your planner or GPS. Free on iOS and Android.
FeaturesTripPlanning.positioningBody: Every rider we talked to had the same problem: planning a real motorcycle trip means juggling five apps. Google Maps for roads, a notes app for stops, a weather app for the pass, a messaging thread for friends, a spreadsheet for fuel budgets. It's friction every step of the way. Trip planning was the first feature we shipped because it's the feature most riders need — and because if we could nail this, everything else about MotoVault would follow from it.
FeaturesTripPlanning.howItWorksTitle: From empty map to saved ride in four steps
FeaturesTripPlanning.step1Desc: Tap the + button in Discover and a full-screen dark map opens, ready for your next adventure. Long-press anywhere to drop a stop, or search for a city, pass, coffee spot or fuel station.
FeaturesTripPlanning.step2Title: Add typed waypoints along the route
FeaturesTripPlanning.step2Desc: Each stop is more than a pin. Choose from ten types — fuel, food, overnight, scenic, photo, mechanical, ferry, pass summit, rally point or a plain stop — and add notes. The stepper groups waypoints by day.
FeaturesTripPlanning.step3Title: Name the trip, set the difficulty
FeaturesTripPlanning.step3Desc: Title, description, start and end dates, difficulty (Easy, Moderate, Challenging, Expert), max riders, and visibility (Private, Unlisted, Public). Every field is optional at first — you can come back and polish before publishing.
FeaturesTripPlanning.step4Title: Keep it as a draft or share the link
FeaturesTripPlanning.step4Desc: Save as a draft to keep iterating. Publish to open invites to friends, or make it public so the community can discover and join your ride. Drafts live in your My Trips, only visible to you.
FeaturesTripPlanning.galleryBody: This is an actual trip built with MotoVault: Bolzano → Passo Sella → Cortina d'Ampezzo → Passo Pordoi → Canazei → Ortisei → Passo Gardena → Bolzano. Eight typed waypoints, three days, rendered on a live map with real road routing.
FeaturesTripPlanning.featuresTitle: The details that make a real trip work
FeaturesTripPlanning.f1Desc: Group waypoints by day. Day 1: Bolzano to Cortina. Day 2: the big passes. Day 3: head home. The app knows which stops belong to which day.
FeaturesTripPlanning.f2Title: Ten waypoint types, from fuel stop to pass summit
FeaturesTripPlanning.f2Desc: Fuel, food, overnight, scenic, photo, mechanical, ferry, pass summit, rally point and a plain stop — each with its own icon on the map and in the itinerary list.
FeaturesTripPlanning.f3Desc: Mapbox Directions computes the actual motorcycle-friendly route between stops. No straight-line approximations — real tarmac, real mileage.
FeaturesTripPlanning.f4Desc: Three visibility levels. Private means only you. Unlisted means anyone with the link. Public means discoverable in the Discover feed.
FeaturesTripPlanning.f5Desc: Organiser invites specific riders, or opens a public trip up to a cap. Each rider can RSVP Going, Maybe or Declined — and pick which bike they're bringing.
FeaturesTripPlanning.f6Desc: Save half-finished trips as drafts. Only you see them. Come back, add the last three stops, then publish when you're ready to share.
FeaturesTripPlanning.f7Desc: Easy, Moderate, Challenging, Expert. So nobody joins an expert pass route thinking it's a Sunday cruise.
FeaturesTripPlanning.f8Desc: Every published trip has a canonical URL. Send it to a group chat, post it to Discord, tweet it — it renders with the route as a preview.
FeaturesTripPlanning.walkthroughTitle: A trip, from first draft to the ride
FeaturesTripPlanning.walkthroughP1: Bolzano goes down first as the Start — "gear check & coffee before departure". Passo Sella drops as a Scenic stop with the note "Iconic Dolomite pass, photo stop". Then Cortina d'Ampezzo as Overnight, Passo Pordoi as Pass Summit, Canazei as Fuel, Ortisei as Overnight, Passo Gardena as Scenic, Bolzano as End. The app groups them into Day 1, Day 2 and Day 3.
FeaturesTripPlanning.walkthroughP2: Named "Dolomites Loop — 3 Days", rated Moderate, capped at 8 riders, it sits as a Private draft until a better overnight in Ortisei is swapped in. Then visibility goes to Public and the trip is live on Discover, with the itinerary in a sheet that slides up over the map.
FeaturesTripPlanning.walkthroughP3: They name it — "Dolomites Loop — 3 Days" — write a description, pick Moderate difficulty, set max riders to 8, and leave visibility as Private. Save as draft. They go back to their garden for coffee. Later that evening they remember a better overnight in Ortisei, swap it in, toggle visibility to Public, and hit Publish. The trip is now live on Discover; two riding friends join by the end of the night.
FeaturesTripPlanning.walkthroughP4: That's the whole arc — from blank map to joined trip — and it runs on real Mapbox routing, real Postgres rows, and a bottom sheet that slides up to show the itinerary without losing the map. No spreadsheets, no screenshot chains, no lost pins.
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq0Question: Does the app actually route on real roads, or does it draw straight lines?
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq0Answer: Real roads. Between any two waypoints, we call Mapbox Directions with motorcycle-friendly routing and render the actual polyline you would ride. Zoom in on any segment of the Dolomites Loop above — you can see the hairpins.
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq1Question: Can I plan a trip before I invite anyone?
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq1Answer: Yes. Every trip starts as a draft, visible only to you. You can build and edit it across multiple sessions, and only publish when you are ready to share.
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq2Question: What happens if I invite people and only half of them can make it?
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq2Answer: Each rider RSVPs Going, Maybe or Declined, and picks which bike they are bringing. You see the count in the trip header (for example, 0/8 riders) and the full list of participants below.
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq3Question: Can I plan a trip that covers multiple countries or crossings?
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq3Answer: Yes. There are no borders in the map — add a Ferry waypoint for a Mediterranean crossing or a Pass Summit for a mountain crossing. The routing engine handles anything Mapbox can route.
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq4Question: How many waypoints can one trip have?
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq4Answer: There's no hard cap you would hit in normal use. The real constraint is readability — past 15 or 16 stops on a single day the itinerary gets busy. Split into multiple days to keep it clean.
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq5Question: Can I export the trip to another app?
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq5Answer: Yes. Export the trip as a GPX file from the trip screen and import it into your planner or GPS. Every published trip also has a web link with a route preview; share it from the trip screen and viewers do not need the app.

FeaturesMaintenance.title: Motorcycle maintenance tracker: service history and reminders
FeaturesMaintenance.description: Log every service, set mileage and time-based reminders, and keep a full maintenance history for every motorcycle in your garage. Free on iOS and Android.
FeaturesMaintenance.heroSubtitle: A service history per bike, with reminders by distance or date that reach you before the work is due.
FeaturesMaintenance.f1Desc: Set reminders by mileage interval, time interval, or both. MotoVault notifies you before service is due — not after it's overdue — and resets automatically when you log the task.
FeaturesMaintenance.f2Desc: Every job is logged with date, mileage, cost, category, notes, and photos. Build a documented timeline for each bike that increases resale value and simplifies insurance claims.
FeaturesMaintenance.f3Desc: A sportbike and a cruiser have different needs. Configure independent maintenance schedules for every motorcycle in your garage.
FeaturesMaintenance.longFormTitle: Motorcycle maintenance tracking that keeps your bike healthy
FeaturesMaintenance.longFormIntro: Motorcycle maintenance is a long-term commitment, and missed intervals are expensive. MotoVault's maintenance tracker replaces the shoebox of receipts and the spreadsheet with a single, organized service history per bike — plus reminders that reach you before a service slips.
FeaturesMaintenance.s1Title: Log a job: task, odometer, cost
FeaturesMaintenance.s1Body: Attach photos of parts or receipts to any job. Tasks are organized into overdue, upcoming and completed tabs, so you always know what needs attention next.
FeaturesMaintenance.s2Title: Reminders based on how you actually ride
FeaturesMaintenance.s2Body: Oil every 5,000 mi, brake fluid every 2 years, or both at once. Because reminders are per bike, a daily commuter and a weekend tourer can follow completely different schedules.
FeaturesMaintenance.s3Body: Share a bike's service history as a read-only web link from the app — dates, odometer readings, costs and notes. A documented service history reassures buyers, supports insurance and warranty claims, and can raise resale value.

faq.question: Does MotoVault track maintenance for multiple motorcycles?
faq.answer: Yes. MotoVault gives every motorcycle in your garage its own service history, reminders, and schedule. You can view each bike individually or see an aggregate overview of which bike needs attention next across your whole garage.

faq.question: Can I set custom maintenance reminders?
faq.answer: Yes. Reminders are fully customizable by mileage interval, time interval, or both. Beyond presets like oil changes and chain lubrication, you can create a reminder for any task, configured per bike. When you log the task as done, the next reminder resets automatically.

faq.question: Can I export my motorcycle's service history?
faq.answer: Not yet. You can share a bike's service history as a read-only web link from the app.

faq.question: Is the maintenance tracker free?
faq.answer: Yes. Maintenance tracking is free on iOS and Android. MotoVault Pro adds more bikes, unlimited AI diagnostics and receipt scans, GPX export and offline trip maps. Pro is a monthly or yearly subscription, with a lifetime option; prices are shown in the store and on /pro.

FeaturesExpenses.title: Motorcycle expense tracker: fuel, parts and cost per mile
FeaturesExpenses.description: Track every motorcycle expense by category, see cost-per-mile, and compare spending across bikes and years. Free on iOS and Android.
FeaturesExpenses.heroTitle: Know exactly what your bike costs
FeaturesExpenses.heroSubtitle: Log fuel, service, parts, gear and insurance against each bike and read the true cost of ownership as cost per mile and monthly trends.
FeaturesExpenses.f1Title: Fourteen expense categories, from fuel to taxes and fees
FeaturesExpenses.f1Desc: Log an expense: category, amount, date, bike. Each expense ties to one bike, so multi-bike owners see exactly where the money goes.
FeaturesExpenses.f2Desc: MotoVault calculates cost-per-mile and per-kilometer automatically, so you can compare bikes and understand what each motorcycle really costs to run.
FeaturesExpenses.f3Desc: See year-to-date spending with category breakdowns, monthly trends, and current-year-vs-all-time comparisons — in both metric and imperial units.
FeaturesExpenses.longFormTitle: Motorcycle expense tracking that reveals the true cost of ownership
FeaturesExpenses.longFormIntro: Most riders underestimate what their motorcycle costs because the spending is scattered across fuel receipts, parts orders, and service invoices. MotoVault's expense tracker pulls all of it into one place and turns raw costs into the metrics that actually matter — cost-per-mile, category breakdowns, and year-over-year trends.
FeaturesExpenses.s1Body: Fuel, maintenance, parts, gear, insurance, taxes and fees: fourteen categories, each expense dated and noted. For multi-bike owners, that means you can see which machine is draining your budget and which is cheap to keep.
FeaturesExpenses.s2Body: Cost per mile and per kilometer come from your logged expenses divided by your ride distances, so the figure moves as you ride. It's the single most useful number for deciding whether to keep or sell, and for budgeting the year ahead.
FeaturesExpenses.s3Title: Spot trends before they surprise you
FeaturesExpenses.s3Body: If maintenance costs are creeping up on an older bike, the monthly trend shows it early — in your choice of metric or imperial units.

faq.question: Is the expense tracker free?
faq.answer: Yes. Expense tracking is free on iOS and Android. MotoVault Pro adds more bikes, unlimited AI diagnostics and receipt scans, GPX export and offline trip maps. Pro is a monthly or yearly subscription, with a lifetime option; prices are shown in the store and on /pro.

faq.question: What expenses can I track?
faq.answer: MotoVault has fourteen expense categories: fuel, maintenance, parts, gear, tires, insurance, registration, tolls, parking, modifications, training, accessories, taxes and fees, and other. Each expense is tied to one motorcycle, with date, amount and notes, so spending is organised per bike.

faq.question: Does MotoVault calculate cost-per-mile?
faq.answer: Yes. MotoVault automatically calculates cost-per-mile and cost-per-kilometer from your logged expenses and recorded ride distances, in both metric and imperial units.

faq.question: Can I track expenses for more than one motorcycle?
faq.answer: Yes. Every expense is assigned to a specific bike, and the dashboard lets you compare spending across all the motorcycles in your garage.

FeaturesRides.title: Motorcycle ride tracker: GPS logging and ride stats
FeaturesRides.description: Record every ride with GPS — distance, speed, elevation, and an interactive route map — linked to the right bike in your garage. Free on iOS and Android.
FeaturesRides.heroSubtitle: Every ride is recorded with full GPS — distance, moving time, speed, elevation and the route map — and filed against the bike you rode.
FeaturesRides.f1Desc: Capture distance, duration, moving vs paused time, max and average speed, and elevation gain and loss — rendered as an interactive route map.
FeaturesRides.f2Desc: Each ride includes interactive speed and elevation charts plotted over distance, with per-waypoint altitude, speed, and GPS accuracy.
FeaturesRides.f3Desc: Rides attach to a specific bike, so each motorcycle's mileage and usage sit right alongside its maintenance history and expenses.
FeaturesRides.longFormTitle: Motorcycle ride tracking that connects to the rest of your garage
FeaturesRides.longFormIntro: A ride log is more useful when it's not stranded in a separate app. MotoVault records every ride with full GPS detail and ties it back to the specific motorcycle you rode — so distance, maintenance, and cost all live in one place.
FeaturesRides.s1Title: Rich GPS data on every ride
FeaturesRides.s1Body: Per-waypoint data includes altitude, speed and GPS accuracy, so a route can be read point by point after the ride, with moving time kept apart from the minutes paused at a fuel stop.
FeaturesRides.s2Body: The ride detail screen plots a speed profile and an elevation profile over distance; tap a point for its value. It's an easy way to relive a route and to see how a bike performs — in metric or imperial units.
FeaturesRides.s3Title: Every ride feeds your bike's record
FeaturesRides.s3Body: Each ride adds its distance to the bike's odometer, which keeps mileage-based maintenance reminders accurate and cost-per-mile figures honest.

faq.question: Is ride tracking free?
faq.answer: Yes. GPS ride tracking is free on iOS and Android. MotoVault Pro adds more bikes, unlimited AI diagnostics and receipt scans, GPX export and offline trip maps. Pro is a monthly or yearly subscription, with a lifetime option; prices are shown in the store and on /pro.

faq.question: What data does MotoVault record on a ride?
faq.answer: Each ride captures distance, duration (moving and paused time), max and average speed, elevation gain and loss, and a complete route map, plus per-waypoint altitude, speed, and GPS accuracy.

faq.question: Can I see speed and elevation for a ride?
faq.answer: Yes. Every ride has a speed profile and an elevation profile plotted over distance; tap a point for its value, in metric or imperial units.

faq.question: Do rides connect to my motorcycles?
faq.answer: Yes. Each ride is linked to a specific bike in your garage, so mileage updates automatically and stays consistent with that motorcycle's maintenance and expense history.
